description:
About the Position

UMCG is recruiting a doctoral candidate for a project on teams and networks in district nursing (team en netwerk in de wijkverpleging). The research studies how nursing teams are organised in Dutch neighbourhood care, how professional networks around clients function, and how team composition and collaboration affect quality and continuity of care at home.

The project combines qualitative fieldwork with quantitative analysis of care-organisation data, working closely with district nursing providers and municipal health actors. The candidate will interview professionals, observe team practices, analyse network structures and contribute to design recommendations for the rapidly changing Dutch home-care sector. The position is a salaried PhD track under the CAO-UMC collective agreement.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in nursing science, health sciences, organisational science or a related discipline, and have an interest in health-services and workforce research. Because the fieldwork runs in Dutch district nursing organisations, fluency in Dutch is required for interviews and observations, while reporting and publication take place in English. The doctoral training runs through the UMCG's graduate programme with a supervisory team spanning health services research and organisational sociology.

Highlights

  • Team organisation in Dutch district nursing
  • Professional network analysis around home-care clients
  • Qualitative fieldwork combined with quantitative analysis
  • Health-services research on quality and continuity of care
  • Collaboration with care providers and municipal actors
  • Salaried PhD track, CAO-UMC collective agreement

About University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG)

UMCG is one of the largest university medical centres in the Netherlands and the academic hospital of the University of Groningen. It combines patient care with biomedical research and graduate education, organised around research institutes covering neuroscience, oncology, ageing, regenerative medicine and population health. The centre employs PhD candidates and postdocs on salaried contracts under the Dutch collective agreement for university medical centres (CAO-UMC). Research and clinical vacancies, including physician-researcher tracks and technical R&D roles, are published on its recruitment portal werkenbijumcg.nl.
